h1: Working as a brewery health and safety officer
title: Brewery Health and Safety Officer Jobs | Craft Beer School
desc: What a brewery health and safety officer does: the main hazards from CO2 to caustic, permits, audits, training, qualifications and career paths.
teaser: Breweries combine gas, chemicals, heat, pressure and heavy loads. The safety officer makes sure everyone goes home.
standfirst: A brewery is a food factory with pressure vessels, confined spaces and concentrated chemicals. Health and safety officers identify those hazards, set the rules that control them and check the rules are followed. It is a career where good work is measured by what does not happen.
sections:
A brewery health and safety officer is responsible for preventing injuries and ill health. In practice that means assessing risks, writing safe procedures, running permit to work systems, training staff, investigating incidents and auditing compliance. At a large brewery this is a full time role, often in a team. At a small craft brewery it may be one part of an operations manager's job.

The officer works with everyone: brewers, packaging teams, maintenance engineers, contractors and management. Much of the job is persuasion, because a rule that the floor does not believe in will be ignored at 3 AM.
The hazards that define a brewery

• Carbon dioxide. Fermentation produces it in large volumes. It is heavier than air and collects in cellars, pits and tanks. Many occupational limits set the eight hour exposure limit at 5,000 ppm (0.5%). Far higher concentrations can cause unconsciousness quickly.
  • Confined spaces. Fermenters, mash tuns and silos may hold CO2, lack oxygen or have moving parts. Entry needs a permit, isolation, gas testing and a standby person.
  • Chemicals. Caustic soda and acids used for cleaning cause severe burns, especially to eyes.
  • Heat and pressure. Hot wort, steam lines, pressurised tanks and kegs.
  • Machinery and vehicles. Packaging lines, conveyors and forklifts.
  • Manual handling. Malt sacks and full kegs are heavy and awkward.
  • Dust. Milling creates fine grain dust, which can irritate lungs and in the wrong conditions can explode.

Large breweries may add ammonia refrigeration and boilers, each with its own controls.
The systems a safety officer runs

The core tool is the risk assessment: what could hurt someone, how likely and how badly and what controls bring the risk down. Controls follow a hierarchy, from removing the hazard altogether down to personal protective equipment as the last line of defence.

Around that sit the working systems. Permits to work control tank entry, hot work and work on live equipment. Lockout and tagout make sure machines and valves stay isolated during maintenance. Gas detection, alarms and ventilation control CO2. Our guide to ventilation and CO2 safety in cellars covers how that is designed.

Then come training records, contractor induction, regular audits and incident investigation. A good investigation looks for root causes, not someone to blame.

One of the most dangerous moments in a brewery is a tank that looks empty. A fermenter emptied of beer is still full of CO2 unless it has been purged with air and tested. People have died climbing into tanks or leaning through manways to retrieve something dropped. A safety officer insists that no one puts their head inside a tank opening until the atmosphere has been tested with a calibrated meter, every time.

Breweries in India fall under factory, pollution control and fire safety rules, which are framed nationally and administered by states. Larger factories must appoint qualified safety officers under state rules, with thresholds and requirements that vary. Check the current notifications for your state rather than relying on another plant's practice.

Common routes into the role include a degree or diploma in engineering or science followed by a postgraduate diploma in industrial safety, or international certificates such as those from NEBOSH. Experience in food, beverage, chemical or pharmaceutical plants transfers well, since the hazards overlap.

Technical knowledge gets you hired. The rest of the job depends on credibility with the floor. Officers who understand the brewing process, why brewers need to open that valve or enter that tank, write procedures that work in practice. Those who do not end up with paperwork nobody follows.

Learn the process. Know why a fermenter builds pressure, what CIP does and why brewers are in a hurry when a lauter is running. It makes every conversation easier and every rule more realistic.

Contractors deserve special attention. Equipment installers, welders and refrigeration engineers come in for short jobs, often in a hurry and unfamiliar with the site. Many serious incidents involve contractors. A short site induction, a permit for any hot work or tank entry and a named brewery contact for each job close most of that gap.

Communication matters as much. Toolbox talks, clear signage, short procedures in the languages your team reads and the habit of thanking people who report near misses all build a safety culture.

Safety officers progress to site safety manager, then to regional or group health, safety and environment roles. Many combine safety with environmental duties such as effluent, energy and water. Others move into consultancy, auditing several plants.

Walk through a brewery or picture one you know. List every place CO2 could collect. Then ask how anyone would know it was there. If the answer is "they would smell it", you have found the first hazard to fix, because CO2 has no reliable smell at dangerous levels.
faqs: What does a brewery health and safety officer do?
Assesses risks, writes safe procedures, runs permit to work systems, trains staff, investigates incidents and audits safety across the brewery.
What is the biggest hazard in a brewery?
Carbon dioxide from fermentation is among the most serious, because it collects unseen in tanks, cellars and pits. Confined space entry, chemicals and machinery are also major hazards.
What qualifications does a brewery safety officer need in India?
Usually an engineering or science degree or diploma plus an industrial safety qualification. Requirements under state factory rules vary, so check the current notification.
